components.note: 马 (horse) — horses and riding: 骑 ride, 驾 drive, 驶; 骄 was a tall spirited horse, then proud.
乔 (qiáo) is a near sound match for jiāo; also in 桥 qiáo and 娇 jiāo.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 傲 is a proud person.
敖 (áo) is a near sound match for ào; also in 熬 áo.

example.hanzi: 父母为她的成绩感到骄傲。
example.pinyin: Fùmǔ wèi tā de chéngjì gǎndào jiāo'ào.
example.english: Her parents feel proud of her grades.
example.fact: 骄傲 can describe either a warm, positive pride (为...骄傲, “proud of...”) or a prickly, negative arrogance (太骄傲, “too arrogant”) depending entirely on context — English keeps these apart as two different words, “proud” and “arrogant,” while Chinese lets one word carry both, leaving tone of voice and context to do the disambiguating.

examples.hanzi: 我为我的家乡感到骄傲。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wèi wǒ de jiāxiāng gǎndào jiāo'ào.
examples.english: I feel proud of my hometown.

examples.hanzi: 取得好成绩后不要骄傲。
examples.pinyin: Qǔdé hǎo chéngjì hòu búyào jiāo'ào.
examples.english: Don't get arrogant after getting good grades.

components.note: 而 (and, but) — oldest form is a beard (compare 须 xū, beard), later borrowed for the conjunction; 而 survives in 耐 nài.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.pinyin: Tā bú shì lǎoshī, érshì xuésheng.
example.english: He isn't a teacher, but rather a student.
example.fact: 而是 never appears alone — it is the fixed second half of the construction “不是...,而是...” (“not X, but rather Y”), used to correct a false assumption about what something is; dropping the 不是 half and saying just “而是” in isolation would sound grammatically incomplete to a native speaker.

examples.hanzi: 我不想去，而是想在家休息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng qù, ér shì xiǎng zài jiā xiūxi.
examples.english: I don't want to go, but rather want to rest at home.

examples.pinyin: Wèntí bú zài tā, ér shì zài wǒ.
examples.english: The problem isn't him, it's me.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.

example.pinyin: Zhè duì nǐ yǒulì.
example.english: This is to your advantage.
example.fact: 利 means advantage and sharp, and so also profit: 利息 (interest), 利润 (profit). 顺利 (smooth) and 胜利 (victory) are staples, and 利弊 ("advantage and drawback") means pros and cons.

examples.hanzi: 这个办法对大家都有利。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ duì dàjiā dōu yǒu lì.
examples.english: This approach benefits everyone.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen de shēngyi hěn shùnlì.
examples.english: Their business is going smoothly.

components.note: 片 (slice, plank) — marks flat pieces and wooden boards; 牌 is a signboard, a card or a tile.
卑 (bēi) hints at the sound: 牌 pái is close to 脾 pí, which shares it.

example.pinyin: Tāmen zài dǎ pái.
example.english: They're playing cards.
example.fact: 牌 is a card, tile or sign: 打牌 (play cards or mahjong), 扑克牌 (playing cards), 招牌 (shop sign), 门牌 (house number plate). As a brand it appears in 品牌 and 名牌 (famous brand).

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen chángcháng dǎ pái.
examples.english: We often play cards on weekends.

examples.hanzi: 他在门口挂了一块牌子。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài ménkǒu guà le yí kuài páizi.
examples.english: He hung a sign at the door.

components.note: 八 (eight) — originally two strokes pulling apart, meaning divide; that sense is in 分 divide, 公 public and 半 half.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bā diǎn qǐchuáng.
example.english: I get up at eight o'clock.
example.fact: 八 is a lucky number because it sounds like 发 (fā, "to prosper"). The Beijing Olympics opened on 8 August 2008 at 8:08 pm for this reason. Phone numbers and car plates with 8s sell at a premium.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yígòng yǒu bā kǒu rén.
examples.english: There are eight people in my family.

examples.hanzi: 八月是夏天最热的时候。
examples.pinyin: Bāyuè shì xiàtiān zuì rè de shíhou.
examples.english: August is the hottest time of the summer.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 他是我们团队的重要成员。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen tuánduì de zhòngyào chéngyuán.
example.english: He is an important member of our team.
example.fact: 员 is Mandarin's general-purpose “person who does/belongs to X” suffix — the same 员 shows up in 演员 (“actor”), 服务员 (“waiter, attendant”), and 教员 (“instructor”) — 成员 simply attaches it to 成 (“to form, to constitute”) for “a person forming part of” a group.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā yǒu sì ge chéngyuán.
examples.english: There are four members in our family.

examples.hanzi: 新成员明天会加入我们。
examples.pinyin: Xīn chéngyuán míngtiān huì jiārù wǒmen.
examples.english: The new member will join us tomorrow.

meanings: to keep a close watch over

components.note: 皿 (dish) — oldest form: a person bending over a basin of water to see a reflection; 鉴 jiàn (mirror) adds metal. To look closely, to supervise.
见 (see) — seeing and looking, as in 现, 觉, 看: 视 is to look.
礻 here is 示 (shì), the altar radical in 礼 and 神: in 视 it is the exact sound clue.

example.hanzi: 这栋大楼一直被监视着。
example.pinyin: Zhè dòng dàlóu yìzhí bèi jiānshì zhe.
example.english: This building has been under surveillance the whole time.
example.fact: 监视 carries a distinctly watchful, often suspicious connotation — closer to English “surveillance” or “keeping tabs on” someone than neutral “watching” — which is why it shows up around security cameras, stakeouts, or parental suspicion, rather than casually watching a movie (that's just plain 看).

examples.hanzi: 商店里装了摄像头来监视小偷。
examples.pinyin: Shāngdiàn lǐ zhuāngle shèxiàngtóu lái jiānshì xiǎotōu.
examples.english: The shop installed cameras to keep watch on thieves.

examples.hanzi: 护士在监视病人的情况。
examples.pinyin: Hùshi zài jiānshì bìngrén de qíngkuàng.
examples.english: The nurse is monitoring the patient's condition.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 这家公司有很多女性员工。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yǒu hěn duō nǚxìng yuángōng.
example.english: This company has many female employees.
example.fact: 女性 is the more formal, clinical register for “female” (used in demographics, medicine, official forms), while 女人 is the plain, everyday word for “woman” — much like English distinguishes “female” from “woman” by formality rather than meaning, Chinese draws the same register line between 女性 and 女人.

examples.hanzi: 这位女性是我们的经理。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi nǚxìng shì wǒmen de jīnglǐ.
examples.english: This woman is our manager.

examples.hanzi: 现在越来越多的女性出来工作。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài yuè lái yuè duō de nǚxìng chūlái gōngzuò.
examples.english: Nowadays more and more women go out to work.

components.note: 木 (wood) — originally 權, the sliding weight of a steelyard scale: weighing, then power; 又 is just a simplification stand-in.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.

example.hanzi: 每个人都有受教育的权利。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu shòu jiàoyù de quánlì.
example.english: Everyone has the right to receive an education.
example.fact: 权利 (“a right, an entitlement”) is a common homophone trap alongside 权力 (also quánlì, “power, authority”) — same pronunciation, same tones, a different second character (利 “benefit” vs 力 “force”) and a genuinely different meaning, so context alone has to do the disambiguating in speech.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu quánlì bǎochí chénmò.
examples.english: You have the right to remain silent.

examples.hanzi: 这是我们的权利，也是我们的责任。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen de quánlì, yě shì wǒmen de zérèn.
examples.english: This is both our right and our duty.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说, 话, 请; 谎 is a spoken lie.
荒 (huāng) sounds the same as 谎 huǎng except for tone; also 慌 huāng.

example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi yǒu shíhou huì shuōhuǎng.
example.english: Little kids sometimes tell lies.
example.fact: 谎 on its own already means “a lie” (as in 谎言, “a false statement”), so 说谎 is literally “to speak a lie” — a transparent verb-object compound, the same simple building pattern behind 说话 (“to speak words”) and 唱歌 (“to sing a song”).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú huì duì nǐ shuōhuǎng.
examples.english: I won't lie to you.

examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuǎng de shíhou, liǎn huì hóng.
examples.english: His face turns red when he lies.

components.note: 圣 (holy) — traditional 聖 had an ear 耳 and a mouth 口: the sage who listens and speaks wisely.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech: 说, 话, 请; 诞 first meant big talk, then birth and birthday.
延 (yán) is only a loose sound hint for dàn.

example.pinyin: Shèngdàn kuàilè!
example.english: Merry Christmas!
example.fact: 圣诞 is short for 圣诞节 (“Holy Birth Festival”) — 诞 alone means “birth,” so the word literally names the holiday after a birth, the same 诞 that shows up in 诞生 (“to be born”) and, per this dictionary entry, historically also in the birthdays of other revered figures, including Confucius.

examples.pinyin: Shèngdàn jié nǐ yào zuò shénme?
examples.english: What will you do at Christmas?

examples.hanzi: 商店里挂满了圣诞礼物。
examples.pinyin: Shāngdiàn lǐ guàmǎnle shèngdàn lǐwù.
examples.english: The shops are full of Christmas gifts.

components.note: 灬 (fire dots) — fire and heat: 热, 点, 煮, 照; 黑 is soot and smoke from a flame.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他是一位来自美国的黑人演员。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi láizì Měiguó de hēirén yǎnyuán.
example.english: He is a black actor from America.
example.fact: 黑人 is built literally from “black” (黑) + “person” (人), paralleling 白人 (“white person”) as Mandarin's basic vocabulary for describing race by skin color — a plainer, more literal naming convention than the more varied and evolving racial terminology English has developed.

examples.hanzi: 这位黑人歌手唱歌特别好听。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi hēirén gēshǒu chànggē tèbié hǎotīng.
examples.english: This singer sings especially beautifully.

examples.hanzi: 他对隔壁新来的黑人邻居很友好。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì gébì xīn lái de hēirén línjū hěn yǒuhǎo.
examples.english: He is friendly to the new neighbor next door.

components.note: 言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查这起案件。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ ànjiàn.
example.english: The police are investigating this case.
example.fact: 警方 refers to “the police” as an institution or authority (as in news reports: 警方表示..., “police stated that...”), while 警察 names the individual officers themselves — similar to English “police” (the force) versus “a police officer” (a person), except Chinese marks the distinction with two entirely different words rather than one word doing double duty.

examples.hanzi: 警方提醒市民注意安全。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng tíxǐng shìmín zhùyì ānquán.
examples.english: The police reminded citizens to be careful.

examples.hanzi: 警方已经找到了失踪的小孩。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng yǐjīng zhǎodàole shīzōng de xiǎohái.
examples.english: The police have found the missing child.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.pinyin: Tā míngnián yào qù Fǎguó liúxué.
example.english: He's going to France next year to study abroad.
example.fact: 法 in 法国 is a phonetic borrowing, not a meaning-based translation — it approximates the sound of “France” (from the older, fuller transliteration 法兰西, Fǎlánxī), the same strategy behind 美国 (“America,” from 亚美利加) and 德国 (“Germany,” from 德意志) — most country names in Chinese are built this way, sound-first, then shortened to one syllable plus 国 (“country”).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qùguo Fǎguó liǎng cì.
examples.english: I have been to France twice.

examples.pinyin: Fǎguó de miànbāo hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: French bread is delicious.

components.note: 毛 (hair) — a picture of a tuft of hair or fur; used in 毛巾 and 毛病 (a flaw).

example.pinyin: Zhè zhī māo de máo hěn ruǎn.
example.english: This cat's fur is very soft.
example.fact: 毛 is body hair and fur. In money, colloquially, 毛 is one tenth of a yuan: 五毛 is fifty fen (the written form is 角). It also means rough or crude: 毛病 (a fault), and Mao is a common surname.

examples.hanzi: 他的毛衣是用羊毛做的。
examples.pinyin: Tā de máoyī shì yòng yángmáo zuò de.
examples.english: His sweater is made of wool.

examples.pinyin: Tā yì máo qián yě bú yuànyì huā.
examples.english: He doesn't want to spend even a single cent.

components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metals, as in 钱 money, 铁 iron, 铜 copper; 错 first meant to inlay metal.
昔 (xī) is a loose sound clue for cuò; 昔 also sounds out 借 jiè, 措 cuò and 惜 xī.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen chàdiǎn cuòguò le huǒchē.
example.english: We almost missed the train.
example.fact: 错过 combines “mistake, wrong” (错) with the directional complement 过 (“to pass, go past”) — literally “to wrongly pass by” — the same 过 that turns a plain verb into “go past it” shows up in 走过 (“to walk past”) and 路过 (“to pass by”).

examples.pinyin: Bié cuòguò zhè ge hǎo jīhuì.
examples.english: Don't miss this great chance.

examples.hanzi: 他错过了最后一班地铁。
examples.pinyin: Tā cuòguòle zuìhòu yì bān dìtiě.
examples.english: He missed the last subway.

components.note: 言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 说 say, 问 ask; 告 is "to tell". 告 also gives sound to 造 zào and 靠 kào.

example.hanzi: 老师警告他不要再迟到。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī jǐnggào tā búyào zài chídào.
example.english: The teacher warned him not to be late again.
example.fact: 警告 sits alongside 告诉 as two of several everyday compounds built on the root 告 (“to inform, announce”) — 警告 adds 警 (“alert, alarm”) to sharpen 告 into a formal caution, distinct from the neutral information-sharing of plain 告诉.

examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jǐnggào wǒ búyào áoyè.
examples.english: The doctor warned me not to stay up late.

examples.hanzi: 警察向司机发出了警告。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá xiàng sījī fāchūle jǐnggào.
examples.english: The police issued a warning to the driver.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.pinyin: Lǎotiān, zhè yě tài qiǎo le ba!
example.english: Good heavens, what a coincidence!
example.fact: 老天 is a casual, spoken stand-in for “Heaven” as an impersonal, fate-controlling force rather than any specific deity — closer in flavor to English “Good God!” or “Heavens!” as an exclamation of surprise than to a formal religious reference; the solemn, formal term for the cosmic Heaven is simply 天, and adding 老 (here an informal, affectionate prefix, as in 老朋友) tips the register toward the colloquial.

examples.pinyin: Lǎotiān bǎoyòu nǐ!
examples.english: May Heaven protect you!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de lǎotiān, zhème duō rén!
examples.english: Good heavens, so many people!

components.note: 吉 (jí) — lucky; as a part it sounds out 结 jié and 洁 jié.

example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ jíxiáng rúyì.
example.english: I wish you good fortune and all you desire.
example.fact: 吉 means lucky, as in 吉利 and 吉祥. Chinese people choose a 吉日 (auspicious day) for weddings and openings. It is also used for sound in transliterations such as 吉他 (guitar).

examples.hanzi: 今天是个吉日，很多人结婚。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì gè jírì, hěn duō rén jiéhūn.
examples.english: Today is a lucky day, and many people are getting married.

examples.pinyin: Zhège shùzì hěn jílì.
examples.english: This number is very lucky.

components.note: 心 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 想, 怒, 思; 惹 stirs up anger or trouble.
若 (ruò) hints at the sound: 惹 rě is close to 诺 nuò.

example.pinyin: Bié rě tā, tā píqi bù hǎo.
example.english: Don't provoke him, he has a bad temper.
example.fact: 惹 is to provoke or cause: 惹麻烦 (cause trouble), 惹事 (stir up trouble), 惹不起 (can't afford to offend). Interestingly 惹人喜欢 means "lovable", as it attracts people's affection.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié rě māma shēngqì.
examples.english: Don't make Mom angry.

examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi zǒngshì rě máfan.
examples.english: This kid is always causing trouble.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks and flavors: 醉 drunk, 醒 sober, 酸 sour, 配 match; 酒 is liquor, with 氵 for the liquid.
酉 also hints at the sound: yǒu is close to jiǔ.
广 (building, shelter) — houses and shops: 床, 库, 座; 店 is a shop.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound hint; same part in 站 zhàn and 战 zhàn.

example.hanzi: 我们订了市中心的一家酒店。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dìng le shìzhōngxīn de yì jiā jiǔdiàn.
example.english: We booked a hotel in the city center.
example.fact: 酒店 literally means “wine shop” (酒 “alcohol” + 店 “shop”) and once named exactly that, but in modern Mainland usage it has drifted to mean primarily “hotel” — a word whose original, dictionary-first sense has been almost entirely displaced by a newer, now-dominant one in everyday speech, while Taiwan usage keeps a “hostess club” sense alive as yet another branch of the same drift.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn lí jīchǎng hěn jìn.
examples.english: This hotel is very close to the airport.

examples.pinyin: Jiǔdiàn de zǎocān hěn fēngfù.
examples.english: The hotel's breakfast is very rich.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 抽 is to pull out.
由 (yóu) — near sound — 抽 is chōu; 由 also sounds out 油 yóu and 邮 yóu.

example.pinyin: Tā bù chōu yān.
example.english: He doesn't smoke.
example.fact: 抽 is to pull something out: 抽烟 (smoke, literally "draw smoke"), 抽奖 (draw a prize), 抽血 (draw blood), 抽屉 (drawer) and 抽空 (to squeeze out some time).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng cóng chōuti lǐ chōu yì zhāng zhǐ.
examples.english: Please pull a sheet of paper out of the drawer.

examples.hanzi: 他的工作太忙，没时间抽烟。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gōngzuò tài máng, méi shíjiān chōuyān.
examples.english: He's too busy at work to have time to smoke.

components.note: 之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".
米 (rice, grain) — the top. Memory aid: grains of rice sorted by size 大 — sorted into groups, a kind (人类). Not proven etymology.
類 (traditional) — used for 'kind, class' with 犬 and 页. 类 is the simplified shape and keeps only a fragment of it.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢苹果、香蕉之类的水果。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan píngguǒ, xiāngjiāo zhīlèi de shuǐguǒ.
example.english: He likes fruits like apples, bananas, and so on.
example.fact: 之类 always closes out a list with 的 attached (“...之类的”), functioning much like English “etc.” or “and so on,” but grammatically it patches onto the last item as though it were itself modifying the following noun — a structural pattern (“A、B之类的C”) with no single-word English equivalent.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢运动，像游泳、跑步之类的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan yùndòng, xiàng yóuyǒng, pǎobù zhīlèi de.
examples.english: I like sports, things like swimming and running.

examples.hanzi: 你可以买些书之类的做礼物。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ mǎi xiē shū zhīlèi de zuò lǐwù.
examples.english: You can buy some books or the like as a gift.

components.note: 王 (king) — three bars for heaven, people and earth joined by a vertical: the ruler who links them. As 玉 jade with its dot dropped it also marks jewels: 球, 玩.

example.pinyin: Shīzi shì sēnlín zhī wáng.
example.english: The lion is the king of the forest.
example.fact: 王 is a king, and 王 is also one of the most common Chinese surnames. It can mean the top of a kind: 歌王 (king of song), and the radical 王 also appears in jade-related characters, where it is a form of 玉.

examples.pinyin: Tā de míngzi jiào Wáng Míng.
examples.english: His name is Wang Ming.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen bān de xiǎo wángzǐ.
examples.english: He is the little prince of our class.

components.note: 冖 (cover, cloth) — things that cover: 写 write, 军, 冥; 冠 is a hand 寸 placing a cap 冖 on a head 元.
车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.

example.hanzi: 她赢得了这次比赛的冠军。
example.pinyin: Tā yíngdé le zhè cì bǐsài de guànjūn.
example.english: She won the championship in this competition.
example.fact: 冠 by itself means “crown, cap” (pictured by its components 冖, headwear, over 元, a head, with 寸, a hand, putting it on) — 冠军 traditionally named the foremost, “crowned” unit or commander in an army, a martial origin that has since broadened from armies to any competition's top finisher.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen duì déle guànjūn!
examples.english: Our team won the championship!

examples.pinyin: Tā shì shìjiè guànjūn.
examples.english: He is a world champion.

meanings: to try (to see what it's like or whether one can do it)

components.note: 尚 (shàng) gives the -ang sound; also in 常 cháng, 偿 cháng, 堂 táng. The old form showed 旨 "tasty".
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 读 read; testing often involves questions.
式 (shì) sounds exactly like 试 — a reliable sound clue.

example.hanzi: 他决定尝试一种新的学习方法。
example.pinyin: Tā juédìng chángshì yì zhǒng xīn de xuéxí fāngfǎ.
example.english: He decided to try a new way of studying.
example.fact: 尝 alone already means “to taste” (as in 尝一尝, “have a taste”) — 尝试 extends that literal sense of testing something by taste into the abstract idea of “trying” any new method or experience, a metaphor from mouth to mind that English's “try” (from Old French, “to sift, select”) arrived at along a completely different route.

examples.hanzi: 你可以尝试用不同的方法。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ chángshì yòng bùtóng de fāngfǎ.
examples.english: You can try using a different method.

examples.hanzi: 我想尝试一下新的工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chángshì yíxià xīn de gōngzuò.
examples.english: I'd like to give a new job a try.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 线; 练 first meant boiling silk to soften it, then practice.
柬 (jiǎn) is a loose sound clue; same part in 炼 liàn and 简 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 我们的篮球教练很严格。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de lánqiú jiàoliàn hěn yángé.
example.english: Our basketball coach is very strict.
example.fact: 练 alone means “to practice, to train” (as in 练习, “to practice”), and adding 教 (“to teach”) gives 教练 both a verb sense (“to coach”) and, more commonly today, a noun sense (“a coach/trainer”) — most often heard as a job title shouted across a sports field rather than used as a verb.

examples.pinyin: Jiàoliàn dài wǒmen liànxí yóuyǒng.
examples.english: The coach takes us to practice swimming.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài xuéxiào dāng zúqiú jiàoliàn.
examples.english: He works as a soccer coach at the school.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ chángcháng qù nà jiā kāfēidiàn.
example.english: I often go to that coffee shop.
example.fact: 常 means usual and often: 常常 (often), 经常 (frequently), 平常 (ordinary), 正常 (normal), 日常 (everyday). Both 常常 and 经常 are common, with 常 alone slightly more concise.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de dōngtiān chángcháng xià xuě.
examples.english: It often snows here in winter.

examples.pinyin: Tā bù chángcháng chídào.
examples.english: He is not often late.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào duìfāng shì shéi.
example.english: I don't know who the other person is.
example.fact: 对方 is a relational noun — it only means anything in reference to “this side” of an interaction (a conversation, a deal, a match), never naming a person the way a name or “he/she” would; English's closest match, “the other party,” carries the same built-in relational logic but sounds notably more formal or legal than 对方 does in everyday Mandarin.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ tīngting duìfāng de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: Please listen to the other side's thoughts.

examples.pinyin: Duìfāng méiyǒu jiē diànhuà.
examples.english: The other person didn't answer the phone.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to follow is to move along behind someone.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 有问题可以随时联系我。
example.pinyin: Yǒu wèntí kěyǐ suíshí liánxì wǒ.
example.english: If you have questions, you can contact me anytime.
example.fact: 随时 combines 随 (“to follow, to go along with”) with 时 (“time”) — literally “following the time [as it comes]” — an image of flexibility that maps directly onto its everyday meaning “whenever, at any time,” the same 随 that gives 随便 (“whatever, as you like”) its easygoing sense.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ suíshí lái zhǎo wǒ.
examples.english: You can come to me at any time.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen suíshí zhǔnbèi chūfā.
examples.english: We are ready to set off at any moment.

meanings: to play (a keyed or plucked instrument)

components.note: 弓 (bow) — bows and tension: 张 stretch, 引 draw, 弯 bend; 弹 is to shoot or spring, and a bullet.
单 (dān) is a loose clue for dàn/tán; compare 禅 chán and 蝉 chán.

example.pinyin: Tā huì tán gāngqín.
example.english: She can play the piano.
example.fact: 弹 is read tán for plucking, bouncing or flicking: 弹钢琴, 弹吉他, 弹性 (elasticity). Read dàn, it means bullet or shell: 子弹, 炸弹, so the two readings are worth keeping apart.

examples.pinyin: Tā huì tán jítā.
examples.english: He can play the guitar.

examples.pinyin: Píqiú tán de hěn gāo.
examples.english: The ball bounced very high.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — striking or acting: 教, 放, 政; 敌 is an opponent to strike.
舌 here is a form of 啇 (dí), the sound part; also in 滴 dī and 嫡 dí.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.pinyin: Zài zhànzhēng zhōng, tāmen shì dírén.
example.english: In the war, they were enemies.
example.fact: 敌 alone can function as a verb meaning “to rival, to match” (as in 无敌, “unrivaled, invincible” — literally “no rival”), and combining it with the neutral suffix 人 (“person”) grounds that abstract idea of opposition into a concrete noun, “an enemy.”

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bú shì dírén, shì péngyou.
examples.english: We're not enemies, we're friends.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的敌人最后投降了。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de dírén zuìhòu tóuxiáng le.
examples.english: The enemy in the movie finally surrendered.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 搭 is to put up or join.
荅 (dā) sounds exactly like 搭; also in 答 dá.
木 (wood) — wooden things: 桌, 板, 架; 档 is a wooden shelf for files.
当 (dāng) is a near sound match for dàng; also in 挡 dǎng.

example.hanzi: 他们两个是很好的搭档。
example.pinyin: Tāmen liǎng gè shì hěn hǎo de dādàng.
example.english: The two of them are great partners.
example.fact: 搭 alone carries a sense of “to put together, to piece up” (as in 搭配, “to match, pair up”), and 档 relates to a shelf-like frame or slot — together 搭档 pictures two people slotted together to work as a pair, a word most at home describing comedy duos, business partners, or coworkers rather than romantic partners (that's 伴侣 or 对象).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào yí ge hǎo dādàng.
examples.english: I need a good partner.

examples.hanzi: 他们搭档做生意已经十年了。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen dādàng zuò shēngyi yǐjīng shí nián le.
examples.english: They have been partners in business for ten years.

components.note: 人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".
未 (not yet) — a tree 木 with a new short branch on top, still growing. Compare 末 mò (end/tip), where the top stroke is longer.

example.hanzi: 我从未见过这么美的风景。
example.pinyin: Wǒ cóngwèi jiànguò zhème měi de fēngjǐng.
example.english: I have never seen such beautiful scenery.
example.fact: 从未 is a more literary, formal register of “never” than the everyday 从来没 — 未 by itself already carries “not yet” in classical/written Chinese (as in 未来, “the future,” literally “not yet come”), so 从未 pairs “from [the start]” with that older negation for a slightly bookish, emphatic “never,” most at home in writing or formal speech.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóngwèi qùguo Běijīng.
examples.english: I've never been to Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Tā cóngwèi duì wǒ fāguo píqi.
examples.english: He has never lost his temper with me.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — curtains and tents are cloth; also in 布 cloth, 帽 hat.
长 (zhǎng) gives a close sound; 胀 zhàng shares it and sounds exactly like 帐.

example.pinyin: Chuáng shang guà zhe wénzhàng.
example.english: A mosquito net hangs over the bed.
example.fact: 帐 is a cloth canopy: 帐篷 (tent), 蚊帐 (mosquito net). Money and accounts are now normally written 账 (结账, 账号), and mixing up 帐 and 账 is a common error.

examples.hanzi: 他们在山上搭了一个帐篷。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài shān shang dā le yí gè zhàngpeng.
examples.english: They put up a tent on the mountain.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ jié yíxià zhàng.
examples.english: Please help me settle the bill.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 话.
炎 (yán) is a close sound clue for tán; 炎 also sounds out 淡 dàn and 痰 tán.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng zhǎo tā tánhuà le.
example.english: The principal called him in for a talk.
example.fact: 谈话 carries a more serious or purposeful shade than casual 聊天 (“to chat”) — a 谈话 is more likely to be a formal conversation, an official interview, or a talking-to from someone in authority, while 聊天 is reserved for relaxed, idle chitchat between friends.

examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī xiǎng hé wǒ tánhuà.
examples.english: The teacher wants to talk to me.

examples.hanzi: 我们的谈话持续了一个小时。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de tánhuà chíxùle yí ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: Our conversation lasted an hour.

components.note: 广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān qìwēn sānshí dù.
example.english: The temperature today is thirty degrees.
example.fact: 度 is a degree of temperature or angle (三十度), and also a unit of electricity in everyday use (一度电). It means to spend time in 度假 (take a vacation), and shows up in 温度 (temperature), 速度 (speed) and 过度 (excessive).

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān zǎoshang yǒu èrshí dù.
examples.english: It is twenty degrees this morning.

examples.hanzi: 我们在海边度过了一个愉快的周末。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài hǎibiān dùguò le yí gè yúkuài de zhōumò.
examples.english: We spent a pleasant weekend at the seaside.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the flesh/body radical (月 in 脸, 脚, 肚); 背 is the back of the body.
北 (běi) — near sound — 背 is bèi; 北 originally pictured two people back to back, which is the sense of 背.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de bèi yǒudiǎn téng.
example.english: My back hurts a little.
example.fact: 背 has two readings: bèi (back, behind; to recite from memory, as in 背单词) and bēi (to carry on the back: 背书包). 背景 is background, and 背后 means behind or behind someone's back.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ bèi duìzhe wǒ zhànhǎo.
examples.english: Please stand with your back to me.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān wǎnshang bèi dāncí.
examples.english: I memorize words every night.

components.note: 艹 stands in for 竹 (bamboo) in the traditional 節, bamboo joints: sections, then festivals and knots.

example.hanzi: 春节是中国最重要的节日。
example.pinyin: Chūn Jié shì Zhōngguó zuì zhòngyào de jiérì.
example.english: Spring Festival is China's most important holiday.
example.fact: 节 grew from the segment of a bamboo stem to mean a festival (节日), a section, and a measure word for class periods and train carriages: 一节课, 一节车厢. 节约 means to economise.

examples.pinyin: Zhè yì jié kè yǒu sìshí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: This class lasts forty minutes.

examples.pinyin: Zhōngqiūjié wǒmen huí lǎojiā guò.
examples.english: We go back to our hometown for the Mid-Autumn Festival.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and binding, as in 红, 给, 经: an agreement binds like a cord.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for yuē; 勺 also in 药 yào and 钓 diào.
羽 (feather) — wings and feathers: 翅 wing, 翼, 习; 翰 was a feather pen, hence writing.
倝 (gàn) is a loose sound clue; same part in 韩 hán.

example.hanzi: 约翰是我在美国认识的朋友。
example.pinyin: Yuēhàn shì wǒ zài Měiguó rènshi de péngyou.
example.english: John is a friend I met in America.
example.fact: 约翰 is a transliteration built purely for sound, not meaning — 约 (yuē) and 翰 (hàn) were chosen to approximate “John” phonetically, the same strategy behind most foreign personal names rendered into Chinese, where the characters' own literal meanings (“to agree” + “a writing brush”) are just irrelevant background noise.

examples.pinyin: Yuēhàn shì yì míng Yīngyǔ lǎoshī.
examples.english: John is an English teacher.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi Yuēhàn ma?
examples.english: Do you know John?

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — arranging and moving by hand: 打, 推, 拉; 排 is to line things up.
非 (fēi) is a loose sound hint; its series includes 悲 bēi and 菲 fēi.

example.pinyin: Qǐng pái hǎo duì.
example.english: Please line up.
example.fact: 排 is a row (第一排, the first row; 一排座位) and the action of arranging: 排队 (queue), 排名 (ranking), 排除 (rule out). 排骨 is spare ribs and 排球 is volleyball.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen páiduì mǎi piào ba.
examples.english: Let's queue up to buy tickets.

examples.pinyin: Tā zuò zài dì-yī pái.
examples.english: He sits in the first row.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: giving permission is spoken.
午 (wǔ) is only a loose sound clue for xǔ.
多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".

example.hanzi: 公园里有许多美丽的花。
example.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu xǔduō měilì de huā.
example.english: There are many beautiful flowers in the park.
example.fact: 许多 sits at a more formal, written-register notch above the everyday 很多 (“a lot of”) — both mean roughly “many,” but 许多 shows up more often in writing or narration, while 很多 is the default choice in casual conversation.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu xǔduō péngyou.
examples.english: I have a lot of friends.

examples.hanzi: 许多人喜欢在周末睡懒觉。
examples.pinyin: Xǔduō rén xǐhuan zài zhōumò shuì lǎnjiào.
examples.english: Many people like to sleep in on weekends.

meanings: (genre of traditional Chinese painting) figure painting

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 这部小说里的人物都很有趣。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù xiǎoshuō lǐ de rénwù dōu hěn yǒuqù.
example.english: The characters in this novel are all very interesting.
example.fact: 人物 leans toward someone notable or narratively significant — a historical figure, a fictional character, a “personage” — rather than an ordinary, unremarkable person, which is why 大人物 (“VIP, big shot”) feels natural but calling a random stranger on the street 人物 would sound oddly weighty.

examples.hanzi: 他是历史上的重要人物。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì lìshǐ shàng de zhòngyào rénwù.
examples.english: He is an important figure in history.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事里有三个主要人物。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge gùshi lǐ yǒu sān ge zhǔyào rénwù.
examples.english: There are three main characters in this story.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.hanzi: 他是我们这个小组的头儿。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen zhège xiǎozǔ de tóur.
example.english: He's the head of our group.
example.fact: 头儿 is a colloquial, spoken-Mandarin word for “boss, leader” — the 儿 here isn't the diminutive “little” sense it carries in words like 女儿 (“daughter”), but rather Beijing-flavored speech's habit of adding a rhotic -r ending to certain nouns, signaling a casual, streetwise register that the plainer, more formal 领导 (“leader”) doesn't carry.

examples.pinyin: Tóur ràng wǒmen xiān kāihuì.
examples.english: The boss told us to hold a meeting first.

examples.pinyin: Nǐmen tóur zài nǎr?
examples.english: Where is your leader?

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling and speech: 吗, 喊, 呼; 叫 is to shout.
丩 (jiū) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 纠 jiū.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 作. 做 is a later variant of 作 zuò (to do), sharing its meaning and sound.
故 (gù) is only a loose sound hint.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shuǐguǒ jiàozuò huǒlóngguǒ.
example.english: This kind of fruit is called dragon fruit.
example.fact: 叫做 functions almost interchangeably with plain 叫 in most contexts (这个叫什么? “What's this called?”), with 做 adding a slightly more formal, explanatory weight — useful when introducing a term or definition rather than just casually naming something, similar to the difference between English “called” and “known as.”

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé jiàozuò Huáng Hé.
examples.english: This river is called the Yellow River.

examples.hanzi: 你为什么把他叫做哥哥？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ wèishénme bǎ tā jiàozuò gēge?
examples.english: Why do you call him older brother?

components.note: 犭 (animal; 犬 dog) — marks animals, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat; 猪 is the pig.
者 (zhě) — close sound: 猪 zhū. 者 also sounds out 煮 zhǔ and 著 zhù.

example.pinyin: Tā jiā yǎng le hěn duō zhū.
example.english: His family raises many pigs.
example.fact: 猪 is the pig, the last animal of the zodiac. Unqualified 肉 means 猪肉 (pork) in China, and 小猪佩奇 is the Chinese name of the cartoon Peppa Pig.

examples.pinyin: Nóngchǎng lǐ de zhū hěn kě'ài.
examples.english: The pigs on the farm are very cute.

examples.hanzi: 你又吃又睡，真像一只小猪！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yòu chī yòu shuì, zhēn xiàng yì zhī xiǎozhū!
examples.english: You do nothing but eat and sleep, just like a pig!

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 激 is water surging up, then to stir up.
敫 (jiǎo) is only a loose sound clue for jī.

example.pinyin: Wǒ fēicháng gǎnjī nǐ de bāngzhù.
example.english: I'm very grateful for your help.
example.fact: 感激 is a noticeably stronger, more heartfelt “thank you” than the everyday 谢谢 — it names the deep emotional state of gratitude itself (感, “to feel,” + 激, “to be stirred up”) rather than performing the social ritual of thanking, so it shows up in earnest, sometimes formal expressions of appreciation rather than a quick “thanks” in passing.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn gǎnjī lǎoshī de bāngzhù.
examples.english: I'm very grateful for the teacher's help.

examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ, wǒ yǒngyuǎn gǎnjī nǐ.
examples.english: Thank you, I'll be grateful to you forever.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to follow is to move along behind someone.

example.pinyin: Qǐng suí wǒ lái.
example.english: Please follow me.
example.fact: 随 is to follow or go along with: 随着 (along with), 随时 (at any time), 随身 (carried on one's person) and 随手 (without extra effort, as in 随手关门, "close the door as you go"). 随便 means "as you like" and is one of the most-used words in casual conversation.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ suíbiàn zuò, búyòng kèqi.
examples.english: Sit anywhere you like; no need to be polite.

examples.pinyin: Tā suízhe yīnyuè tiào qǐ wǔ lái.
examples.english: He started dancing along with the music.

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.pinyin: Tā zài Zhōngguó gōngzuò le wǔ nián.
example.english: He worked in China for five years.
example.fact: 中国 literally means “the central/middle country” (中 “middle” + 国 “country”) — reflecting an ancient worldview in which China saw itself as the civilizational center; the same 中 shows up in 中间 (“in between”) and 中午 (“midday”), all sharing that core sense of “the middle.”

examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó de Chūnjié hěn rènao.
examples.english: Spring Festival in China is very lively.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xué Zhōngguó cài.
examples.english: I want to learn to cook Chinese food.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — a picture of an ox's head with horns; as a radical it marks cattle, in 牺, 牲, 牧, 物.

example.pinyin: Nóngmín yǒu yì tóu niú.
example.english: The farmer has an ox.
example.fact: 牛 counts with 头 (一头牛). In slang 牛 means impressive: 你真牛！ ("you're awesome"). It forms 牛肉 (beef) and 牛奶 (milk).

examples.hanzi: 这头牛每天吃很多青草。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tóu niú měitiān chī hěn duō qīngcǎo.
examples.english: This cow eats a lot of grass every day.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de zì xiěde zhēn niú!
examples.english: Your handwriting is awesome!
